result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided by borders, beliefs, cultures, or identities. I would replace it with a shared understanding that we are all interconnected, that every person’s suffering and joy ripple through the whole, and that our collective well-being depends on recognizing this truth.

This shift wouldn’t erase differences—cultures, histories, and perspectives would still thrive—but it would dissolve the artificial walls that justify exploitation, conflict, and indifference. We’d see that harming others is harming ourselves, that healing one is healing all, and that the systems we’ve built to divide us are the very chains we’ve mistaken for freedom.

It’s not about uniformity; it’s about unity in diversity. And it starts with the quiet revolution of seeing the stranger as kin.
